newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bankers suspend peso volatility band.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bankers suspend peso volatility band.

text.p: The Bankers Association of the Philippines said on Monday it was suspending until further notice its 1-1/2 percent peso volatility band.
It is also changing Philippine Dealing System trading hours to 9 am to 4 pm (0100-0800 gmt) from the usual 8.30 am to 5.30 pm (0030-0930 gmt).
"Effective today (the Association) has suspended the volatility band until further notice," it said in a statement.

Under the Association rules which govern local bank currency trading, trading is suspended if the peso moves 1-1/2 percent either side of the weighted average rate which is based on the previous day's close.

Under the rule, the peso should have started trading on Monday at 26.40 to the dollar, despite having plunged last Friday 11.5 percent to 29.45 pesos after the Central Bank allowed an effective devaluation by letting the currency trade in a wider bands.
Traders had warned that if the volatility band had been kept the market would have been thrown into confuson.
Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson told Reuters on Sunday night that he had asked the Association to drop the band.
But he added: "I will still be in the market...We will come in to calm down the market."
Traders expect the peso to open at around 29 to 30 per dollar.
